Technical & price structure: In plain terms: Egypt Aluminum is the country’s only primary-aluminium smelter — Nag Hammadi turns an administered electricity price into LME dollars, carries ~EGP 9bn of net cash, and in May 2026 signed a US$900m Trafigura partnership to roughly double capacity toward ~600 kt. Marked lens by lens the business is worth ~EGP 250 a share; at 286 the price pre-pays part of that doubling and a record FY25/26 close. The whole argument is whether the power contract holds and the financing actually signs.
Monte Carlo — where could the price go?: 50,000 paths, 16 forces: the stock\'s own calibrated secular drift (the master variable), the LME aluminium price, the EGP, the industrial electricity tariff, EGX flows, alumina costs, CBAM, the Trafigura financing, the FY25/26 results and dividend, a possible MIH stake-sale, and global risk appetite. FAQ: What is the fair-value range for Egypt Aluminum (EGAL)? — testahil publishes a probability distribution of where EGAL could trade over the next 1–3 months — the simulated 5th–95th percentile range and the central 50% — not a single price target or a buy/sell call. The full study and open model show the methodology. This is educational analysis, not investment advice.

How is the EGAL valuation calculated? — The study uses an instrument-appropriate lens — a consolidated FCFF discounted cash flow for Egypt's sole primary-aluminium producer, cross-checked on replacement cost per tonne of capacity, global smelter multiples and normalized mid-cycle earnings — combined with a 50,000-path Monte Carlo simulation that expresses the result as a probability distribution. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.

Does testahil recommend buying or selling EGAL? — No. testahil never issues buy, sell, or hold recommendations. It publishes fair-value ranges and probability distributions as educational material, and grades its own forecasts publicly when they resolve.
